title: "You're overreacting"
topic: Difficult team dynamics and conflict between colleagues
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on the postnatal ward. Mrs Jones, 31, gave birth two hours ago. Her blood pressure is now 86/50 and her heart rate 122, and her pad is soaked.

You ask the midwife to call the obstetric registrar. She says, "You're overreacting. Let's give it half an hour."
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Ask the labour ward coordinator to tell the midwife to call the registrar.
options.detailed: This may work, but it delays getting senior help when you could call yourself.

options.text: Wait half an hour and reassess, as the midwife suggests.
options.detailed: If she is bleeding, half an hour could be life-threatening. It is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Explain calmly to the midwife why you're concerned.
options.brief: Shares your reasoning and keeps the team working together.
options.detailed: Explaining the observations may change her view, and you will need her help. It ranks second because calling for help comes first.

options.text: Bleep the obstetric registrar yourself straight away.
options.brief: She may be bleeding seriously, so a senior is needed now.
options.detailed: Low blood pressure, a fast heart rate and heavy bleeding after birth suggest a postpartum haemorrhage. You don't need the midwife's agreement to call for help. It ranks first.

options.text: Discuss the disagreement with the midwife once Mrs Jones is stable.
options.brief: Helps the team learn from it.
options.detailed: A later conversation can help you both understand each other's views. It ranks third because it is not urgent.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you escalate a deteriorating patient despite a colleague's disagreement.
explanation.keyDetails: She has signs of a postpartum haemorrhage. The midwife disagrees. You can call the registrar yourself.
explanation.reasoning: [D] gets help now, [C] keeps the team together, and [E] addresses the disagreement later. [A] delays help, and [B] could be fatal.
explanation.competing: Some would explain to the midwife first, to keep her on side. With these observations, calling for help can't wait, and you can explain while you wait for the registrar.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 1, recognising and responding to deterioration.
